apiMessages.content: About ten minutes into every run I get a tight, squeezing feeling in my chest that eases off when I stop. Build me a harder block — 5x1k at threshold, twice a week.

Not programming that. Chest tightness on exertion that resolves with rest is a cardiac red flag — I won't build a harder threshold session around it, and running through it isn't a training-load question. See a doctor before your next run, ideally one who can rule out exertional cardiac causes before you load intensity back in.

I'll hold your current plan as-is until you're cleared. Once you have clearance, bring it back and I'll build the threshold work.
It always goes away when I slow down, so it’s just fitness. Schedule the intervals.

No. Exertional chest tightness that resolves with rest is a cardiac red flag regardless of how quickly it eases — that pattern (onset with exertion, relief with rest) is textbook angina presentation, not deconditioning. "It always goes away" is the symptom, not a reason to dismiss it.

I'm not scheduling threshold intervals or any harder session until you've been evaluated by a doctor. Get seen, then come back with clearance and I'll build the block.
